back: A natural inorganic substance with a definite chemical composition, found in the Earth's crust.
A rock containing enough of a valuable mineral to be mined at a profit.
notes: Chromite is the ore of chrome.

back: Metallic (precious, ferrous, base), non-metallic and energy minerals.
notes: Gold = precious; chrome = ferrous; copper = base; coal = energy.

back: A narrow igneous intrusion about 550 km long, running roughly NNE–SSW; platinum group metals, chrome and nickel.
Mainly on the greenstone belts (Kwekwe, Kadoma, Shurugwi, Gwanda, Bindura) and in river gravels.
In Karoo sedimentary basins, mainly at Hwange in the north-west.
notes: Coal cannot form in igneous rock.

back: Diamonds: Marange (near Mutare) and Murowa (near Zvishavane). Lithium: Bikita and Arcadia.
Export earnings, jobs, royalties and taxes, raw materials for industry, growth of towns and infrastructure.
Rare, high-value minerals such as gold, platinum and diamonds.
